contract: predict_shift(training_profiles, training_perturbations, query_perturbations, gene_context) -> finite query x gene matrix of expression shifts relative to controls. Whole perturbation groups are disjoint. Minimize query MSE divided by error of training-perturbation-mean baseline; report mean-reference-corrected perturbation retrieval.
notes: Independently written bounded scientific adaptation. Source data and SHA256 preparation receipts required. See docs/BIOLOGY_EXPANSION.md and task limitations; fixture tests never establish source benchmark reproduction.

name: Biology: Perturb-seq response generalization
description: Predict expression shifts for complete held-out genetic perturbations using measured GEARS study pseudobulks and training-only gene selection.

sources.locator: GEARS Methods: data processing, perturbation splits and combinatorial prediction.
Official author implementation/data reference; evaluator and seed are independently written, not copied.
Systema: correcting shared perturbation effects and reporting perturbation-specific evaluation.

limitations: Independent training-mean-normalized error and retrieval metric inspired by Systema; not the entire published GEARS/Systema metric suite. Official Dataverse source access returned403 during preparation.
Public source subsets are development-visible. Freeze candidates before evaluating on additional independently chosen studies/instances; trusted candidate execution is not a security sandbox.
Improving this benchmark is a scientific-method result; it does not alone establish a new biological discovery.

papers.title: Predicting transcriptional outcomes of novel multigene perturbations with GEARS
papers.primary_goal: Predict expression responses to previously unmeasured single- and multigene perturbations.
papers.task_relation: The local task uses measured GEARS study pseudobulks and holds out complete perturbations. It tests a reduced gene-expression prediction problem rather than reproducing the paper's full network or all multigene results.

Using a task to evaluate an agent, framework, or general-purpose model, or citing only a benchmark, dataset, or tool, does not establish scientific importance.
